summary: Not established. Apple's website terms bar automatic programs from accessing its sites, so the page was not captured, and nothing in this repository shows the sign-in markup or whether it sits in a frame on another origin. The profile stays manual.

sources.title: Apple Website Terms of Use, section Your Use of the Site
International portal profiles: what an earlier read of the Apple entries returned

staysInteractive.note: Apple's identity verification on a trusted device; named by the repository's profile text, never exercised.

lookedFor: Apple Website Terms of Use, read in full. They cover www.apple.com and all associated sites linked to it by Apple, and state: You may not use any deep-link, page-scrape, robot, spider or other automatic device, program, algorithm or methodology to access, acquire, copy or monitor any portion of the Site. The capture tool is such a program, so https://account.apple.com/ was not captured.

robots.txt of account.apple.com: it allows the root path and disallows /account/, /settings/ and /auth/, and it answers HTTP 403 to a client without a browser-style user agent. It was not the reason for skipping the capture.
docs/international-portal-profiles.md item 1: an earlier static read of account.apple.com returned the page title and no application body, so the sign-in is drawn by script.

This repository: no fixture, adapter, test or route catalog names an Apple sign-in control, a frame or an identity origin. The only identity host named anywhere is idmsa.apple.com, as the redirect target of the developer account entry (the same document, item 2).
The frame question. The plan records as recollection, not as a finding, that the sign-in fields sit in a frame served from another origin. Nothing read here confirms or refutes it.
Apple's help and developer pages were not read: they belong to the sites the terms cover, and help pages show screenshots, not markup.
neededFromUser: The sign-in page saved from the user's own browser as "Webpage, Complete", read with --from-file. Its top document shows whether the fields are in the page or in a frame and names the frame's address. If they are in a frame, that frame's own document saved the same way is needed as well. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: If the fields prove to be in a frame on another origin, the steps format cannot express the login: a step's frame is same-origin only, and releasing a credential into a cross-origin frame is question Q8, not approved. Until then no steps file is written under any evidence.
